subject: modify either subplot labels or subplot orders

messages.author: 99e3ad08a7577760
messages.subject: modify either subplot labels or subplot orders
parts:
Hi,
I am rather new to ggplot environment. I have been trying without success to modify the order of the subplots (which is automatically set alphabetically if I use prov_name which gives me the right title but the wrong order) obtained via facet_wrap, while I want it to be geographical (prov_geoorder, which gives me the right order but the wrong titles). Is there a way to change the order of subplots in facet_wrap or at least to change the titles of the subplots?
 
here is my code:
PTFR <- subset(data, (ORDER ==11) &(PTFR>0))
p <- ggplot(PTFR, aes(year,PTFR))
p <-   p+geom_point(colour="darkblue",size=I(1))
p <-   p+geom_smooth(se=FALSE,colour="blue",method="loess")
p <-   p+ggtitle("Total Period Fertility Rate")
p <-   p+xlab("")
p <-   p+ylab("")
p <-   p+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(colour="grey",size=6,angle=0,hjust=.5,vjust=.5,face="plain"),
                 axis.text.y = element_text(colour="grey",size=6,angle=0,hjust=1,vjust=0,face="plain"))
p <-   p+facet_wrap(~prov_name,ncol=6)
p <-   p+theme(strip.text.x = theme_text(size = 8, colour = "black", angle = 0))
p <-   p+opts(plot.title=theme_text(size=20))
p

Thank you for any suggestion,

Ale

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: modify either subplot labels or subplot orders
parts:
Hi:

I am not enamored of the name 'data' for data frames, so I did a
little rewriting of your code. (Try data() at the prompt to see why.)
Basically, you need to define a factor with reordered levels. You also
mixed the old and new theming systems in your code, so I modified that
as well. The first line in theme() shows how the new theming system
applies inheritance of theme properties.

library(ggplot2)
DF <- read.csv("copy.csv", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

DF$prov_geo <- factor(DF$prov_name)
DF$prov_geo <- with(DF, reorder(prov_geo, prov_geoorder, mean))

PTFR <- subset(DF, (ORDER ==11) &(PTFR>0))

p <- ggplot(PTFR, aes(year,PTFR))
p + geom_point(colour = "darkblue", size = 1) +
geom_smooth(se = FALSE, colour = "blue", method = "loess") +
labs(title = "Total Period Fertility Rate",
x = "", y = "") +
theme(axis.text = element_text(colour="grey", size=6, angle=0,
face = "plain"),
axis.text.x = element_text(hjust=.5, vjust=.5),
axis.text.y = element_text(hjust=1, vjust=0),
strip.text.x = element_text(size = 8, colour =
"black", angle = 0),
plot.title = element_text(size=20)) +
facet_wrap(~ prov_geo, ncol=6)


Dennis

2013/4/23 Dennis Murphy <djm...@gmail.com>
Hi:

It looks as though you need to get acquainted with the subset() function:

... + geom_point(data = subset(PTFR, year < 1975 & year > 2011),
                           aes(year, PTFR), colour = "red", size = 2)  +
...

The syntax for subset is, in general,
subset(data_frame, logical condition to select rows, select =
c(<variables to keep>))

See ?subset for a complete description of the function with some examples.

Dennis
